sentences.text: The skull of Acynodon is extremely brevirostral, meaning it has a small and broad snout compared to other alligatoroids.
Its osteoderms, the bony plates embedded in the skin, possess a distinctive double keel structure.
A. adriaticus is the only species of Acynodon for which articulated postcranial material is preserved in at least two specimens.
Acynodon was first described in 1997 and initially placed within the family Alligatoridae.
Histological analysis of a specimen's dorsal rib shows a thickened cortical layer and at least 31 Lines of Arrested Growth (LAGs) despite the specimen being somatically immature.
Acynodon first appeared in the lower Campanian of the Late Cretaceous and disappeared during the mass extinction at the K-T boundary.
The time range for Acynodon is from the Campanian to the Danian, approximately 83.6 to 61.66 million years ago.
